L16: ## 110.67 Being projective is not local on the base
L17: 
L18: In the chapter on descent we have seen that many properties of morphisms are local on the base, even in the fpqc topology. See Descent, Sections 【11†35.22】, 【12†35.23】, and 【13†35.24】. This is not true for projectivity of morphisms.
L19: 
L20: 【14†Lemma 110.67.1.】 The properties
L21: 
L22:   1. $\mathcal{P}(f) =$“$f$ is projective”, and
L23: 
L24:   2. $\mathcal{P}(f) =$“$f$ is quasi-projective”
L25: 
L26: are not Zariski local on the base. A fortiori, they are not fpqc local on the base.
L27: Proof. Following Hironaka [Example B.3.4.1, 【15†H】], we define a proper morphism of smooth complex 3-folds $f:V_ Y\to Y$ which is Zariski-locally projective, but not projective. Since $f$ is proper and not projective, it is also not quasi-projective.

L16: ## 110.68 Non-effective descent data for projective schemes
L17: 
L18: In the chapter on descent we have seen that descent data for schemes relative to an fpqc morphism are effective for several classes of morphisms. In particular, affine morphisms and more generally quasi-affine morphisms satisfy descent for fpqc coverings (Descent, Lemma 【11†35.38.1】). This is not true for projective morphisms.
L19: 【12†Lemma 110.68.1.】 There is an etale covering $X\to S$ of schemes and a descent datum $(V/X,\varphi )$ relative to $X\to S$ such that $V\to X$ is projective, but the descent datum is not effective in the category of schemes.
L20: 
L21: Proof. We imitate Hironaka's example of a smooth separated complex algebraic space of dimension 3 which is not a scheme [Example B.3.4.2, 【13†H】].

L32: Let $S$ be a Noetherian affine scheme. Let $S'\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes. Let $X\to S$ be a morphism such that $X_{S'}\to S'$ is projective. Is $X\to S$ projective? It is not difficult to see that this holds when $S'\to S$ is a field extension.
L33: 
L34: The analogous statement for proper morphisms is true because being proper is fpqc local on the base. Hironaka's examples show that the same argument can not work for projective morphisms.
